findings.title: Public group member pages now truncate at 50 members with no way to continue
findings.body: `Group#findMembers` is shared by the public group-members route and now always sends its new default `limit` of 50. The public `group/members` template has no pagination controls or offset handling, so visiting a visible group with more than 50 members permanently displays only the first 50. Either keep the public request unpaginated or add public pagination before applying this limit.

findings.title: Legacy PATCH membership updates now silently hide groups
findings.body: `resources :groups` still routes PATCH requests to `update`, but the previous PATCH-specific handling of `changes[:add]` and `changes[:delete]` has been removed. A previously supported request such as `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with only `changes: { add: "user" }` now ignores the membership change and, because it has no top-level `visible` parameter, executes this line and sets `visible` to false. Existing API clients or admin automation can therefore fail to update membership while unintentionally hiding the group; preserve the PATCH behavior or explicitly reject it without changing attributes.

findings.title: Pagination creates an empty extra page for exact page-size member counts
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For a group with exactly 50, 100, etc. members, this reports one page too many. The enabled Next action then requests an offset equal to `user_count`, and the server correctly returns an empty member list, leaving administrators on a blank page. This calculation should use a ceiling (while retaining the zero-member special case).

findings.title: The public group-members endpoint changes its top-level JSON contract
findings.body: Previously `GET /groups/:group_id/members` rendered a serialized array of users. It now returns an object with `members` and `meta` keys. The bundled client was changed accordingly, but any existing API consumer that parses the endpoint as an array will break immediately. Preserve the old response on the existing endpoint or introduce/version a paginated response contract.
